In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization, crystallization and structural determination of human recombinan cyclooxygenase 2, the inducible isozyme of cyclooxygenase.
the elucidation of the three-dimensional structures of human cyclooxygenase isoforms.
the structural characterization of the COX-2 active site, which will be the starting point to design new selective COX-2 inhibitors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are able to obtain crystals of COX-2 in a complex with a potent and selective inhibitor, that the structure of the enzyme-inhibitor complex will help to understand the mechanism of action of this class of drugs and that it will provide a structural basis for the design of novel inhibitors with higher specificity for COX-2 and thus reduced side effects.
the COX-2 crystallographic work is in progress and we expect to have the structure of COX-2 in the near future.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the COX-2 protein can be purified and reconstituted to form a functional enzyme.
COX-2, like COX-1, is a dimeric enzyme, and that the dimeric nature of the enzyme may play an important role in the catalytic cycle.
it is possible to obtain crystals of a membrane-bound protein in a detergent environment, and that the crystals are suitable for high-resolution structural studies.
